column1: # The places of prostration — مواضع السجدة.
# `sajdah` is the concept and has its dictionary entry. These are its
# members: the points at which the reader prostrates, each marked in the mushaf
# by the sajdah sign and the rule drawn above the word that makes it due.
# WHAT IS VERIFIED, AND HOW
#   * The set of surahs. al-Itqan's chapter on the etiquette of recitation names
#     all 14 — al-Araf, al-Rad, al-Nahl, al-Isra, Maryam, al-Hajj,
#     al-Furqan, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, Sad, Fussilat, al-Najm, al-Inshiqaq (named
#     by its opening words) and al-Alaq — and states the count as 14.
#     Checked against the book, not recalled.
#   * The count of places. The project's own mushaf registry records 15
#     places drawn as thirty shapes, a sign and a rule at each. Fifteen against
#     al-Itqan's 14 is not a contradiction: the surahs are 14 and
#     the places are 15, because al-Hajj carries two.
#   * Every ayah number is checked against the surah's verified Kufi count in
#     registries/ayah_counts.tsv, so a reference outside its surah cannot pass.
#     Two of them fall on the last ayah of the surah — al-Najm and al-Alaq —
#     which the counts confirm independently.
# WHAT IS STILL NOT VERIFIED: no source in this repository enumerates the
# 15 ayah numbers themselves. The surah is attested and the number is
# inside its surah, and that is all that can be said. Check each against
# al-Bayan or against the mushaf before this file leaves draft.
# THE ONE OPEN QUESTION IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT OURS: at al-Naml the mushaf
# registry carries the sign and the rule in two separate groups bearing two
# different ayah numbers, 27:24 and 27:26. That is recorded there as unresolved
# and is left unresolved here.
# `ayah` is a reference in the KUFI numbering, the one the Madinah mushaf
# prints. In another school the same place carries a different number, which is
# what registries/ayah_numbering.tsv and ayah_counts.tsv are for. `surah` is a
# code from registries/surahs.tsv.
# `ruling` records that the number of places is a difference between the
# schools of law, not between the reciters: they agree on where the words are.
# `agreed` marks a place every school counts; `disputed` marks one that some
# schools do not count, which is why the set is also given as 14 places rather
# than 15.
# `azimah` is a different fact: عَزَائِم السُّجُود is the technical name of the
# subset held to be emphatic, and the schools differ over which places are in
# it. The column is `yes`, `no` or blank; blank means no source in this
# repository has been checked for it yet.
